sections.h2: Which Knox County offices deal with a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Five phone numbers cover nearly every Knox County tax question, and they all lead to the Barbourville courthouse complex at 401 Court Square. The valuation office sets the number, the sheriff collects against it, the clerk inherits whatever goes unpaid, and the county attorney chases it from there.

Knox County contacts, from the Kentucky Department for Local Government county listing
OfficeUse it forPhone
Property valuation administrator (PVA)Value, exemptions, appeal conferences(606) 546-4113
SheriffPaying the current bill(606) 546-3181
County clerkDeeds, delinquent certificates, filing an appeal(606) 546-3568
County attorneyDelinquent bills and payment talks(606) 546-9515
Fiscal courtGeneral county government(606) 546-6192

The courthouse opens at half past eight and closes at four on weekdays. The clerk's office and the circuit clerk's office also see the public on Saturday mornings until noon. Anyone filing a deed for a Knox County house takes it to the clerk on the courthouse's first floor.

sections.h2: What kind of place is Knox County for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Knox County is mountain country in the southeast corner of Kentucky, 388 square miles bordered by Clay, Bell, Whitley and Laurel counties. Barbourville, the seat, lies in the valley where Richland Creek meets the Cumberland River, and U.S. 25E carries traffic about 16 miles northwest to Corbin and the same distance southeast to Pineville. Corbin is mostly across the line in Whitley County. Artemus and Flat Lick are the other named communities.

The county dates from December 19, 1799, carved out of Lincoln County. The present courthouse, finished in 1964, is the fifth to serve it. Coal built the local economy, and unlike much of the coalfield the county kept most of its jobs and people. Health care, retail and schools now employ the most workers. Barbourville is home to Union Commonwealth University and to the Daniel Boone Festival each October.

Population stood at 30,193 in the 2020 census and an estimated 29,532 in July 2025, down 2.2 percent. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 numbers for the county:

  • Owners put the middle home at $118,700.
  • 65.3 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, among 11,711 households.
  • Rent in the middle runs $681 a month.
  • The middle household earns $32,527 a year.
  • The Bureau lists no building permits for 2025.

With values at that level, a tax bill reflects a smaller base than in neighboring counties, and a few hundred dollars owed in back taxes can be a large share of what a sale brings.

sections.h2: Which school district sits on a Knox County bill?
sections.html:
Three public districts operate inside the county line. Knox County Public Schools covers the whole county, Barbourville Independent serves the city of Barbourville from a single campus for grades preschool through 12, and Corbin Independent serves Corbin, which makes it one of the few Kentucky districts that crosses a county line. Lynn Camp, Central, Girdler, Flat Lick and Dewitt are among the schools in the county system.

Which district a parcel belongs to depends on its location, so a buyer comparing two houses a few blocks apart can be looking at different school lines. Ask the PVA or the sheriff which district applies to the parcel number before you quote a price or compare bills.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Knox County assessment?
sections.html:
Start by asking the PVA for a conference. Value is fixed as of January 1, and the roll sits open to the public for thirteen days from the first Monday of May. Kentucky does not allow an appeal without that conference first, and the county's own PVA website says the office values property at full fair market value.

A conference clears the way to file with the county clerk, with a deadline of close of business on the workday after inspection closes. The local board then meets between 25 and 35 days later. Photos, contractor bids, appraisals and sales of similar homes all count as evidence. A board with nothing in front of it denies the appeal. An owner who files and then skips the hearing loses the chance to go on to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

In a county where the middle owner-occupied home is valued at $118,700, a house with a failing roof or a flooded basement is a good candidate to document before May.

sections.h2: When does Knox County want its tax money?
sections.html:
December 31 is the due date for the assessment year, and the sheriff opens collection on either October 1 or November 1 in most counties, according to the Department of Revenue. Discount and penalty dates are printed on the bill, so rely on the Knox County Sheriff's mailing rather than a general table. The sheriff's office can answer at (606) 546-3181.

Collection stops on April 15. Whatever remains unpaid then goes to the county clerk. The debt belongs to the person who owned the property on January 1, and a lien rides along with the parcel for eleven years under KRS 134.420, whoever holds the deed. For a seller, that means the bill follows the closing table, not the person.

sections.h2: What does an unpaid Knox County bill turn into?
sections.html:
A certificate of delinquency recorded as a lien. The county clerk's website offers a delinquent tax search and cautions that the clerk's own figure controls at the time of sale.

The Department of Revenue's worked example shows how a $1,000 bill swells. On transfer it stands at $1,254. A week later, with interest, the clerk's commission and a lien fee, it reaches $1,387.79. After the first county attorney notice it climbs to $1,611.30, and a June advertisement pushes it to $1,659.90.

  • Interest runs at one percent for every month or part of a month.
  • The county attorney sends a 30-day notice, then a second notice within 60 days.
  • The sale date falls 90 to 135 days after transfer, which in a regular-schedule county means mid-July to late August.
  • Advertising runs 30 to 45 days ahead of the sale in the paper and online.
  • A buyer at the sale takes over the lien, and the owner pays that buyer.

sections.h2: Who gets the homestead exemption in Knox County?
sections.html:
People 65 or older, and people classed as totally disabled by a retirement system, can subtract $49,100 from the assessed value of the home they live in, for both 2025 and 2026. They must own and occupy the house on January 1. File with the Knox County PVA by December 31, either online, by mail or in person.

The PVA's website also names exemptions for some religious, educational and government property. A home that passes to heirs who live elsewhere does not keep the exemption automatically, so ask the PVA after a death.

sections.h2: How are taxes divided when a Knox County house sells?
sections.html:
The January 1 owner is on the bill, so a March sale still leaves the seller as the named taxpayer. The settlement statement divides the year, and the closing agent pays the sheriff. KRS 382.135(1)(d) requires the deed to give an in-care-of address for that year's bill, so supply the buyer's mailing address.

Owners who inherited a house, fell behind or manage a vacant rental often ask whether a cash buyer can settle everything at once. The payoff must be known first. Ask the sheriff for the current figure and the county clerk for any older certificate, then ask the county attorney whether a payment plan is on file, since a title company will want that answer.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Knox County?
faqs.a: The Knox County Sheriff takes the current bill, at (606) 546-3181. Once the bill is turned over after April 15, the county clerk at (606) 546-3568 takes payment on the delinquent certificate.

faqs.q: How can I challenge my Knox County property value?
faqs.a: Hold a conference with the PVA at (606) 546-4113, then file with the county clerk by the close of business on the workday after the roll inspection ends. Bring evidence of value.

faqs.q: How much is the Knox County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 off the assessed value for 2025 and 2026, for owners 65 or older or totally disabled who live in the home. Apply at the PVA by December 31.

faqs.q: Does interest apply to late Knox County taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Once the bill reaches the clerk as a delinquent certificate, interest accrues at one percent per month, and commissions and fees are added on top.

faqs.q: Is it possible to sell a Knox County house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: It is. The lien stays on the parcel, so the payoff comes out of the sale proceeds. Collect written figures from the sheriff and the county clerk before setting a closing date.
